explanation: The same fort, taken and then lost. The February article: "On 20 February 1799, the French began their assault, and successfully captured El Arish from the Ottomans. After capturing the fort, the French repaired the fortifications that had sustained damage during the siege." The December article opens on what was left there: "El Arish was garrisoned by 300 French men led by Chef de Bataillon Louis-Joseph Elisabeth Cazals. The Ottoman army consisted of 14,000 men." This is precondition-of. Neither article says the February capture brought on the December attack. The December article gives its own occasion for that, the Grand Vizier's army arriving at Jaffa while negotiations were under way. But the garrison the Ottomans massacred was in that fort because the French had taken and repaired it ten months earlier.
